findings.how: Round 1: describeEntry returned null for every command, remote and wsl entry, and main sent only the newest 150 of the 500 entries the log keeps. copy.ts now writes lines for a command's question, answer, refusal, announcement and end: where it ran, the shell when known, and how it ended, never the command's text. It also writes lines for connections made, lost, ended and failed, and for Ember's helper removed. withCommandShells carries the shell from a command's decision to its answer and its end. main.ts returns recent(500). A disconnect reads 'Ended · Connection to build-01', because the 'Disconnected' tag was cut off in Chromium. Round 2 (verifier): every batch reconnect try got its own 'Didn't work · Connect to build-01' line, about 24 in 10 minutes. connections.ts now marks a reconnect's failed try with reconnect: true and, when onLost gives up, audits {step:'gave-up', host, kind} once. connectionLine hides the marked tries and shows the end as 'Didn't work · Reconnect to build-01 · Ember couldn't reach it.' A connect the user started still has its own line. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §6 says that a reconnect's tries make one line and that the audit keeps each try.

verifierProblems.what: userWords maps every "the user's" to "your", including the possessive at the end of a clause. decide.ts:130 writes the reason "an earlier step in the task wasn't the user's" into every command decision once a task is tainted. What Ember did then shows "Asked you · Run a bash command on build-01 · It asks first: an earlier step in the task wasn't your." I saw this both in an esbuild probe of userWords and in the Chromium render of the built page (run2/dom/activity.mjs). decide.ts:130 is the only audit reason with this shape today.
verifierProblems.fix: In userWords (app/renderer/home/copy.ts), before the general rule, change a "the user's" that is followed by punctuation or the end of the text (e.g. /\b([Tt])he user's(?=\s*[.,;:!?)]|$)/) to "yours". Add decide.ts's exact taint reason to home-activity.test.ts "reasons in your words" (expected: "It asks first: an earlier step in the task wasn't yours.").

verifierProblems.what: The new note is wrong under a policy that turns commands off on SSH. With admin.commands.ssh = "off", local-service returns state "off" and the registry says can "nothing yet". computersView then shows "Connected, commands off" with the note "Turn on commands for build-01 under Commands to use it." In the same window, commandsView shows "Run commands on build-01" disabled, next to "Your organisation has turned off commands on computers reached over SSH." (I checked this with an esbuild probe of computersView and commandsView.) The runtime's own connected bubble already tells this case apart (byAdmin in runtime.ts).
verifierProblems.fix: In computersView, pass modeFor(i.admin, "ssh") into sshStatus. When it is "off", keep the status and give no note, or OFF_LINES.ssh, instead of the "Turn on commands…" hint. Add a home-computers test with admin { source: "x", features: {}, commands: { ssh: "off" } }.

verifierProblems.what: Each failed reconnect now gets its own line in What Ember did. connections.ts doConnect audits {step:"failed", host, kind} on every batch reconnect try. onLost retries at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and then every 30 s for up to 10 minutes, which is about 24 tries. connectionLine shows each one as "Didn't work · Connect to build-01 · Ember couldn't reach it.", so one link that drops for good can take about 24 of the 80 lines and push out task and command lines. That is the crowding #152 is about.
verifierProblems.fix: In connections.ts:618 add `reconnect: true` to the failed audit when mode.reconnect. In copy.ts connectionLine, return null for those entries: the "Lost" line already says it, and one line can be kept for when it gives up. Alternatively, collapse consecutive identical lines in refreshActivity. Add a test.

verifierProblems.what: Copy: the same act now has two names. Settings and the docs call it "Remove helper" / "Remove Ember's helper from build-01" / "Removing Ember's helper…". What Ember did calls it "Didn't work · Remove Ember from build-01" and "Removed · Ember from build-01" (copy.ts connectionLine). This breaks the rule of one name for the same thing everywhere.
verifierProblems.fix: In copy.ts connectionLine, use `Remove Ember's helper from ${name}` for the failed uninstall and `Ember's helper from ${name}` for "Removed". Update the two expectations in home-activity.test.ts.

verifierProblems.what: Weak test. computers-copy.ts matches the registry's exact strings (STALLED_CAN "isn't answering", WSL_OFF_CAN "WSL is off in Ember", NOTHING_CAN "nothing yet"), but only "commands once you agree" is tied to real registry output (buildRegistry in home-computers.test.ts). If the wording in registry.ts changes, the rows silently go back to "Connected: isn't answering" and WSL "Not available", and no test fails.
verifierProblems.fix: Add home-computers tests that build the registry (buildRegistry plus summaryOf) for a stalled link, a distro listed while WSL is off in Ember, and a connected headless host with commands off. Feed the summaries into computersView and expect "Connected, but not answering", "Off" and "Connected, commands off". Alternatively, export the three strings from app/shared/targets.ts and use them in both places.
